NAME: FROZEN PEANUT BUTTER DESSERT
TXT:
Contributed to the echo by: Janice Norman

Steve, my husband, also a peanut butter addict, had a peanut
butter/chocolate dessert this week at a meeting. He enjoyed it so much
that he asked for the recipe. It turns out that it was a combination
of two different recipes. I plan to make it for him soon, and thought
you might like to have it also.

Frosty Peanut Butter Dessert

Crust:

1 cup flour (all purpose)
2 tablespoons sugar
1 stick butter or margarine, melted
1/2 cup chopped walnuts

Mix and press into 13 x 9 pan. Bake at 350 for 15 minutes or until
light brown. Toast 1 small package of coconut. Cool crust and coconut.

Filling:

1 pkg. (8 oz.) cream cheese softened
1/2 c. sugar
1/4 c. peanut butter
1 tsp. vanilla
2 eggs
2 c. frozen whipped topping, thawed
1 c. chocolate chips

Beat cream cheese with sugar, peanut butter, vanilla. Add eggs, one at
a time. Fold in topping. Spread over crust. In double boiler or
microwave oven, melt chocolate chips. Drizzle chocolate in a thin
stream over filling. With a knife, cut through to marble filling.
Cover & freeze.

NAME: LAMB BURGERS W/RASPBERRY-MINT SAUCE
TXT:
Contributed to the echo by: Vincent Mcguire

I am getting ready for a supper this evening, so I thought it was
about time to prepare a grocery list. I thought I'd share the main
course.

Lamb Burgers with Raspberry-Mint Sauce

2 pounds of ground lean lamb
salt and ground pepper
8 ounces of soft mild chevre
Raspberry-Mint sauce

1. Season the ground lamb to taste with salt and pepper, and divide
the meat into 8 burgers.

2. Shape about 1 ounce of the chevre into a round nugget and mold one
part of the lamb around the chevre. Now, mold it into a thick burger.
Repeat with all parts.

3. Make the mint sauce.

4. Broil or grill the burgers. Serve with some of the sauce on the
side.

NAME: RASPBERRY-MINT SAUCE
TXT:
Contributed to the echo by: Vincent Mcguire

Raspberry-Mint Sauce

1-1/2 cups mint leaves
1/3 cup white wine vinegar
2 tablespoons raspberry vinegar
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
3-4 tablespoons superfine sugar
salt and ground black pepper

Tear the mint leaves into coarse pieces and place in a shallow bowl.
Add the vinegars and lemon juice. Stir in the sugar -- amount depends
on desired sweetness -- and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Store covered in refrigerator.
